key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can act as a universal, non-contact fingerprinting tool to identify and quantify grain-boundary defect species in organic halide perovskite solar-cell films.
engineering_relevance: This enables closed-loop defect passivation and quality control for perovskite devices, helping reduce non-radiative losses, ion migration, and degradation that limit efficiency gains.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of sequential-vacuum-evaporated perovskite films.
Match intrinsic phonons and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrations against a THz fingerprint library.
Use oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and guide passivation in real time.
evidence_signal: Across MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3, the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scaled linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting direct quantitative defect sensing.
watch_item: The approach depends on building material-specific THz fingerprints and may be most reliable for films and defects represented in the reference library.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
